title: Best AI Game Generators 2026: 21 Tools Sorted by What They Actually Make
summary: 21 AI game development tools compared by what they actually make: playable games, assets, or design docs. Free tiers, export, and commercial rights verified.
body_markdown:
In 1958, a physicist at Brookhaven National Laboratory wired an analog computer to an oscilloscope so visitors could hit a glowing dot over a net. *Tennis for Two* took a few weeks to build. Four years later, three MIT students spent roughly two hundred hours writing *Spacewar!* on a PDP-1.


In 2026, you can type "a two-player space duel with gravity" and get a playable browser game back in a minute.


The catch is that "AI game generator" now means five different kinds of tools, and most comparisons blend them together. Some make a game you can play. Some make sprites and 3D models. Some help you script inside Unity or Roblox. One makes explorable worlds with no rules at all. Pick from the wrong group and you get beautiful assets with no game, or a playable toy with no way to export it.


> **TL;DR:** We sorted **21 AI game generators by what they actually produce** : playable games (Rosebud AI, Astrocade, Star, Summer Engine), game assets (Scenario, Meshy, Ludo.ai), engine assistants (Unity, Roblox), world models (Google Project Genie), and design docs. Free tiers, export, and commercial rights verified September 22, 2026. Plan the game first with[free game-design generators](https://www.taskade.com/generate/game-development) .


---


## Quick Answer: The Best AI Game Generator by What You Want


**The best AI game generator depends on what you want at the end: a playable game, game assets, help inside an engine, or a design document.** For a playable browser game from one prompt, Rosebud AI is the most complete. For a real engine project you own, Summer Engine (Godot 4) and open-source GDevelop lead. For art, Scenario and Meshy lead. For free, fast prototypes, Claude artifacts and Gemini Canvas are hard to beat.

## What Is an AI Game Generator?


**An AI game generator is a tool that turns a written description into part or all of a video game.** In 2026 the term covers five different products: generators that output a playable game, asset generators that output sprites and models, AI assistants inside game engines, world models that output explorable environments, and design generators that output the documents a game is built from. Only the first group produces something you can play.


The distinction matters because each group hands you something different at the end of an afternoon:


```text
WHAT YOU GET BACK                  EXAMPLE TOOLS                   CAN YOU PLAY IT?
────────────────────────────────   ─────────────────────────────   ────────────────
A playable game (code + art)       Rosebud AI, Astrocade, Star     Yes, in a browser
An engine project you own          Summer Engine, GDevelop         Yes, after export
Game assets (sprites, 3D, audio)   Scenario, Meshy, Ludo.ai        No, you assemble it
Help inside an existing engine     Unity AI tools, Roblox          Only what you build
An explorable world, no rules      Google Project Genie            Explore, not play
A design document                  Taskade game generators         No, it is the plan


```


---


## What a Game Actually Is, and Why a Prompt Can Now Produce One


**A small video game is a loop of states: a title screen, a play state that reads input and updates the world, and an end state that returns to the start.** That loop is short enough to fit in a few hundred lines of JavaScript, which is why a language model can now write one in a single response. The hard part of game design was never the loop. It is what happens inside the play state.


*Tennis for Two* and *Spacewar!* both fit this shape, and so does nearly every browser game an AI tool generates today. The difference in 2026 is who writes it. In 1962 it took a team of students months of evenings. Today a generator writes the loop, draws placeholder art, adds sound, and hosts the result.


Spacewar! running on the Computer History Museum's restored PDP-1. The 1962 game already had the full loop: input, physics, collision, score. Photo: Joi Ito / Wikimedia Commons / CC BY 2.0.


What a generator cannot yet do reliably is the part that made *Spacewar!* worth playing for sixty years: the tuning. How fast the ships turn, how strong the gravity is, how long a round lasts. That is where your time still goes, and it is why the best results come from people who write down what they want before they prompt.


Spacewar! gameplay. Ship speed, turn rate, and the pull of the central star are tuning values, the part of a game that no generator sets well on the first try. Image: Wikimedia Commons / public domain.

## Is the Free Tier Actually Free?

Here is what each free tier produces, verified against vendor pages on September 22, 2026. The honest pattern: **the general assistants are currently the most generous free way to make a small playable game.** Dedicated game generators earn their price when you need longer projects, better art, hosting, or commercial rights.

## Who Owns What You Make?


**Commercial rights to AI-generated games and assets vary by tool and by plan, and free tiers are where the restrictions usually sit.** Before you put a price on a game, check the plan you built it on.


Tool Free-tier rights Paid-tier rights


Rosebud AI No commercial right stated on free Commercial rights and "100% of profits" from the 10x Dev plan ($30/mo)


Star "Users retain ownership of the games and content they create" (terms of service) Same, plus branding-free exports on Pro


Scenario Personal and evaluation use only Full commercial license, resale allowed


Meshy Creative Commons Attribution 4.0: selling allowed with credit Full private ownership


Layer.ai No free tier "Commercial license for all users"


Inworld Free on-demand usage Commercial license on paid tiers


Where a vendor publishes no terms for a tier, we left it out rather than guess. Asset licensing across the whole category remains uneven, so the safest habit is simple: save the terms page on the day you generate the asset you intend to sell.

**Five of the nine game builders below produce 3D output, and seven of the nine offer a way to take the game elsewhere. We found no export for Astrocade or Websim.** The export route is what separates them: a code tab, a project download, a single HTML file, or a real engine project. This matrix was checked against vendor pages on September 22 and 24, 2026.

## How We Compared These Tools


We are a vendor too, so here is exactly how this comparison was built:


- **Every price and free-tier limit** was checked against the vendor's own pricing page or documentation on **September 22, 2026** , and the main game builders were re-checked on **September 24, 2026** . The tool screenshots are headless captures of each public homepage from the same week. Where a page would not load or did not publish a number, we say so instead of quoting a third-party figure.
- **Tools are grouped by what they produce** , not ranked on one scale. A sprite generator and a playable-game generator are not competitors, and scoring them together misleads.
- **We did not run one identical prompt through every tool.** Several products gate generation behind trials or paid plans, which makes a fair single-prompt test impossible without mixing free and paid output. We describe what each tool produces instead of scoring a bake-off.
- **Taskade appears last in the list** , in the design-document category, because that is honestly where it fits. It is not a game engine.
- **Every entry names at least one real strength** , including the tools that compete most directly with each other.


Each tool was checked against the same five questions, in the vendor's own words:


Question What counts as a yes Where we looked


What do you get back? A playable game, an engine project, an asset, or a document Product page and docs


Can you make something on $0? A generation you can keep, not only a demo Pricing page


Can you take it with you? Code, project, or file export Pricing page and docs


Can you sell it? A written commercial right on that plan Terms or pricing page


What does a build cost? A published credit cost per game or per build Pricing page and FAQ

## Playable Game Generators


These tools turn a prompt into something you can play in a browser.


### 1.[Rosebud AI](https://rosebud.ai/) : Best Overall for a Playable Game From One Prompt


[Rosebud AI](https://rosebud.ai/) turns a text description into a complete browser game with code, art, and sound, in 2D or 3D (Three.js and voxel styles). It is the tool most people mean when they search for an AI game maker, and it ranks for nearly every variation of that query.


Rosebud AI homepage, captured September 2026.


**Key features:** prompt-to-game generation; generated JavaScript you can edit by chat, or by hand in a browser Code tab from the Indie Dev plan; one-click publishing that gives you a link anyone can play; 2D and 3D asset generation; a Windows desktop export; a remix community of other creators' games.


**Free plan (re-checked Sep 24, 2026):** the product page says it is free to start, and the pricing page lists its paid plans as "everything in Free, plus" without publishing the Free limits. Third-party reports of the free credit amount conflict. Treat free use as a trial and check your balance before a long session.


**Pros:**


- The most complete prompt-to-playable pipeline in this list
- Code stays editable, so you are not stuck with the first draft
- Publishing to a shareable link takes one click


**Cons:**


- Free-tier limits are not clearly published
- Commercial rights start on the $30 plan, and downloadable project code on the $50 plan


**Pricing:** Indie Dev $15/month with 100,000 credits. Commercial rights and removal of Rosebud branding start at 10x Dev, $30/month. Downloadable project code starts at Pro, $50/month.


**Bottom line:** the best first stop if you want a playable game you can share today.


### 2.[Astrocade](https://www.astrocade.com/) : Best for Sharing Games With a Built-In Audience


[Astrocade](https://www.astrocade.com/) is a social platform where people create small games from prompts and publish them to a public feed that others play and remix. It raised a combined **$56 million Series A and Series B** , led by Sea and Sequoia, announced on **May 5, 2026** , and at the time reported about 5 million monthly active users, roughly 140 million plays a month, and more than 75,000 games.


**Key features:** prompt-to-game creation; a public feed with play counts; remixing other people's games; mobile-first play.


**Free plan (verified Sep 22, 2026):** creating and playing are free. We found no paid consumer tier; the pricing URL returned a 404.


**Pros:**


- A real audience on day one, which almost no other tool offers
- Free to create
- Strong momentum and funding in 2026


**Cons:**


- We found no option to export your game's code
- Output leans 2D in practice


**Pricing:** free.


**Bottom line:** the right choice when you want players more than you want the source code.


### 3.[Star](https://buildwithstar.com/) : Best for Hosted Multiplayer Games You Can Export and Own


[Star](https://buildwithstar.com/) turns a description into a hosted browser game and gives every game its own URL. Its gallery holds both 2D games and 3D games, including first-person shooters. Its terms of service state that users retain ownership of the games and content they create, and you can export to itch.io, Windows, or your own files. You also choose the model behind each build, including Claude models.


Star homepage, captured September 2026.


**Key features:** prompt-to-game with an AI playtesting option; a unique URL per game; multiplayer rooms, leaderboards, and mobile and gamepad controls; export to itch.io, Windows, or your own files; in-game item sales where the creator keeps 70%; a per-build model picker.


**Free plan (re-checked Sep 24, 2026):** playing and sharing are free for everyone, and new accounts build free on the default model with no credit card.


**Pros:**


- Clear ownership terms in plain language
- Export paths to the places indie games actually ship
- Model choice lets you trade speed for quality


**Cons:**


- Branding-free exports and the Windows build need the $50 Pro plan
- Stronger models cost more per build


**Pricing:** Creator $20/month for 3,000 credits, Pro $50/month, or one-time packs from $3 for 300 credits, which Star estimates at about 20 builds on its default model.


**Bottom line:** the best pick when you want a hosted game with multiplayer today and the option to take it elsewhere later.


### 4.[Summer Engine](https://www.summerengine.com/) : Best for a Real Engine Project You Can Ship to Steam


[Summer Engine](https://www.summerengine.com/) builds games on **Godot 4** , so what you get back is a real engine project, not a hosted page. It exports to Steam, mobile, and the web, and it positions itself explicitly as the own-your-code option.


Summer Engine homepage, captured September 2026.


**Key features:** AI-led building on top of Godot 4; a manual editor; exports to Steam, mobile, and web; MCP connection so outside AI tools can work on the project.


**Free plan (verified Sep 22, re-checked Sep 24, 2026):** a free app with a hosted AI trial, the manual editor, export, and MCP access. **AI-powered building itself is on paid plans.**


**Pros:**


- A standard Godot project you can open without Summer Engine
- The clearest path from prototype to a store listing
- The manual editor keeps you in control


**Cons:**


- The AI building you came for is paid
- More setup than a browser-only tool


**Pricing:** Pro $20/month; Pro+ $60/month is recommended for AI-led building; Ultra $200/month.


**Bottom line:** the best choice when the goal is a shipped game, not a shared link.


### 5.[GDevelop](https://gdevelop.io/) : Best Free and Open-Source Game Engine With AI Help


[GDevelop](https://gdevelop.io/) is an open-source, no-code engine for 2D and 3D games with an AI assistant that helps you build mechanics. It is the most generous permanent free plan among dedicated game tools in this list.


GDevelop homepage, captured September 2026.


**Key features:** event-based no-code logic; 2D and 3D; an AI helper for building mechanics; one-click export to desktop, web, and mobile.


**Free plan (re-checked Sep 24, 2026):** $0 with 40 AI credits a month, 3 cloud projects, unlimited publishing to its gd.games web portal, and one desktop and one Android publish per day.


**Pros:**


- Open source, so the engine outlives any subscription
- A permanent free plan, not a trial
- A large library of tutorials and templates


**Cons:**


- The AI assists building; it does not generate a whole game from one prompt
- App Store publishing starts on the Gold plan, and companies with more than $50,000 in yearly revenue must use Pro


**Pricing:** Silver $7.99/month (200 AI credits a week), Gold $13.99/month, and Pro $39.99/month on monthly billing, with up to 40% off on yearly billing.


**Bottom line:** the best free foundation for anyone who wants to learn how games are built.


### 6.[OpenGame](https://opengame.app/) : Best for Downloading a Finished Game File


[OpenGame](https://opengame.app/) , formerly ai-game-generator.com (the old domain now permanently redirects), generates 2D games as a single HTML file and 3D games as a downloadable project bundle.


**Key features:** 2D and 3D generation; a single-file HTML output for 2D; a ZIP project for 3D; an examples gallery.


**Free plan (verified Sep 22, re-checked Sep 24, 2026):** **no free generation.** Examples are free to view; custom builds use paid Studio Credits.


**Pros:**


- The output is a file you keep, with no platform dependency
- Clear, published credit costs per game


**Cons:**


- Nothing to generate for free
- Built for downloads rather than hosted sharing


**Pricing:** Starter $15/month for 80 credits, enough for about 16 2D games or 8 3D games.


**Bottom line:** a clean pick when you want the game as a file and nothing else.


### 7.[Websim](https://websim.com/) : Best for Quick, Playful Experiments


[Websim](https://websim.com/) generates games and small web apps from prompts and publishes them at a public project link. It rewards experimentation: try an idea, share it, and move on.


**Key features:** prompt-to-web-app and game; public project pages; remixing.


**Free plan (verified Sep 22, 2026):** the site says you can create games and apps for free. It publishes no cap.


**Pros:**


- Free and fast
- Public links for every project


**Cons:**


- We found no code export
- No published limits, so heavy use is unpredictable


**Pricing:** not published.


**Bottom line:** a playground for trying ideas, not a production pipeline.

## Free General AI Builders That Can Make a Game


General-purpose AI assistants and app builders are now surprisingly good at small games, and several do it on a free plan.


### 8.[Claude Artifacts](https://claude.ai/) : Best Free Way to Prototype a Game Today


[Claude](https://claude.ai/) can build interactive artifacts: HTML and JavaScript that run live in the chat. Ask for "a Breakout clone with three levels and a high score" and you get a playable game in the side panel. Artifacts are supported on the **free plan** , and sharing by link is free on any plan. The code-execution setting must be turned on.


**Key features:** playable HTML games in chat; iterative edits by conversation; share by link; copy the full source.


**Free plan (verified Sep 22, 2026):** artifacts and public sharing work on the free plan.


**Pros:**


- The most capable free prototype tool in this list
- You can read and keep every line of the code
- Great for learning how a game loop works


**Cons:**


- Long or complex games outgrow a single artifact
- No hosting, assets library, or publishing pipeline beyond a shared link


**Pricing:** free, with paid Claude plans for higher limits.


**Bottom line:** the fastest free way to go from idea to something you can play.


### 9.[Gemini Canvas](https://gemini.google.com/) : Best Free Option on Google's Stack


[Gemini](https://gemini.google.com/) Canvas generates and previews HTML and React prototypes, including small games, and the Canvas feature is available on the free plan. Paid tiers upgrade the underlying model rather than unlocking Canvas itself.


**Key features:** live preview of generated code; edits by conversation; sharing.


**Free plan (verified Sep 22, 2026):** Canvas is included on the free plan.


**Pros:**


- Free, with a live preview
- A long context window on paid tiers for bigger projects


**Cons:**


- Same single-file limits as other chat-based builders
- No asset pipeline


**Pricing:** free; paid Google AI plans upgrade the model.


**Bottom line:** an equal alternative to Claude for quick free prototypes.


### 10.[Replit](https://replit.com/) : Best for Growing a Prototype Into a Real Project


[Replit](https://replit.com/) markets an AI game-building use case for 2D platformers, endless runners, and strategy games, and it gives you a full development environment behind the prompt. When a prototype needs files, packages, and version control, Replit is the natural next step.


**Key features:** an AI agent that builds in a real project; hosting; a full code editor.


**Free plan (verified Sep 22, 2026):** the Starter plan includes one published project; pricing page details did not load for us, so confirm current limits.


**Pros:**


- A real codebase you can keep growing
- Hosting built in


**Cons:**


- Less game-specific than the dedicated tools
- Free usage is tight


**Pricing:** paid Replit plans for more agent usage and deployments.


**Bottom line:** the right home once a quick prototype becomes a project.

## Game Asset Generators


These tools make the parts of a game: art, models, and sound. You still assemble the game in an engine.


### 11.[Ludo.ai](https://ludo.ai/) : Best All-in-One Asset and Ideation Suite


[Ludo.ai](https://ludo.ai/) generates sprites, UI elements, textures, music, 3D assets, and video, and in 2026 it added a **Playable Generator** that prototypes 2D web games on PixiJS. It started as a game-ideation and market-research tool, which still shows in its strengths.


Ludo.ai homepage, captured September 2026.


**Key features:** image, sprite, and UI generation; music and sound; 3D; the 2026 Playable Generator for quick 2D prototypes; API and MCP access.


**Free plan (re-checked Sep 24, 2026):** 30 free credits on signup with no card required; the pricing page shows paid tiers only.


**Pros:**


- The broadest asset range in one subscription
- Ideation tools that help before any art exists
- The new Playable Generator bridges assets and prototypes


**Cons:**


- Free usage is a one-time taste
- Playable prototypes are 2D only


**Pricing:** Indie $15/month billed annually ($180 a year for 3,000 credits up front); Pro $35/month billed annually adds API and MCP access.


**Bottom line:** the best single subscription for a solo developer who needs many kinds of assets.


### 12.[Scenario](https://scenario.com/) : Best for Consistent, Style-Trained 2D Art


[Scenario](https://scenario.com/) trains models on your own art style so every new asset matches the last. It generates 2D images, video, audio, and 3D meshes, with exports for Unity and Unreal.


**Key features:** custom style training; 2D, video, audio, and 3D output; GLB, OBJ, FBX, STL, and VOX export with PBR materials.


**Free plan (verified Sep 22, re-checked Sep 24, 2026):** 50 credits a day, no card required. **Free output is for personal and evaluation use only.**


**Pros:**


- The strongest style consistency in this list
- A full commercial license on paid plans, including resale
- Engine-ready 3D formats


**Cons:**


- Free output cannot be used commercially
- Style training takes setup time


**Pricing:** Starter $15/month for 1,500 credits.


**Bottom line:** the best pick when your game's art must look like one artist made it.


### 13.[Meshy](https://www.meshy.ai/) : Best for 3D Models With Clear Free-Tier Rights


[Meshy](https://www.meshy.ai/) generates 3D models from text or images. Its licensing is unusually clear: free-tier models are published under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0, which allows selling with credit.


Meshy homepage, Games and Media tab, captured September 2026.


**Key features:** text-to-3D and image-to-3D; texturing; multiple export formats.


**Free plan (verified Sep 22, 2026):** 100 credits a month that reset automatically; free models under CC BY 4.0.


**Pros:**


- Commercial use is allowed even on free, with attribution
- Monthly credits reset, rather than a one-time grant


**Cons:**


- Generated meshes usually need cleanup for animation
- Private ownership requires a paid plan


**Pricing:** paid Pro plans for more credits and private ownership.


**Bottom line:** the easiest 3D starting point for an indie game.


### 14.[Tripo](https://www.tripo3d.ai/) : Best Alternative for 3D Asset Generation


[Tripo](https://www.tripo3d.ai/) is a 3D model generator widely compared with Meshy. Reported free-tier credit amounts vary, and its pricing page blocked our direct check, so confirm current limits before relying on it.


**Key features:** text-to-3D and image-to-3D; multiple formats.


**Free plan (verified Sep 22, 2026):** a monthly credit allowance; reports indicate free output is non-commercial. We could not load the pricing page directly.


**Pros:**


- A strong second option for 3D
- Commercial rights on paid plans


**Cons:**


- Free output reportedly cannot be sold
- Limits were not verifiable from the vendor page


**Pricing:** reported Pro plan near $20/month.


**Bottom line:** worth a comparison test against Meshy on your own asset.


### 15.[Layer.ai](https://www.layer.ai/) : Best for Studios Producing Assets at Volume


[Layer.ai](https://www.layer.ai/) generates 2D images, video, 3D models, and audio, with 3D export to Blender and Maya. It is priced for ongoing production rather than casual use.


**Key features:** multi-format generation; 3D export to Blender and Maya; team workflows.


**Free plan (verified Sep 22, 2026):** **no free tier.**


**Pros:**


- The lowest entry price among paid asset tools here
- A commercial license stated for all users


**Cons:**


- No free way to try it
- Unit-based pricing takes planning


**Pricing:** $10/month for 300 Creative Units.


**Bottom line:** a practical production tool for small studios that know what they need.


### 16.[Leonardo](https://leonardo.ai/) : Best for Concept Art and Promotional Images


[Leonardo](https://leonardo.ai/) is a general image generator popular with game creators for concept art, key art, and store-page images. Reports indicate free-tier creations are public and carry no ownership rights, so use paid plans for anything you ship.


**Key features:** image generation with many style models; image-to-image editing.


**Free plan (verified Sep 22, 2026):** a daily token allowance; our direct check of the pricing page was blocked, so confirm the current figure.


**Pros:**


- Excellent for concept art and marketing images
- A wide range of style models


**Cons:**


- Not game-specific
- Free creations are reportedly public and not yours to sell


**Pricing:** reported Essential plan near $12/month.


**Bottom line:** the right tool for the art around your game rather than inside it.


---


## AI Inside Game Engines


### 17.[Unity's AI Tools](https://unity.com/products/ai) : Best for Developers Already Building in Unity

## How to Make a Game With AI in Five Steps


**The fastest route to a good AI-made game is a written design, one playable build, and several small rounds of tuning with real players.** The steps below work with any playable-game builder in this list. The design stage is where most first-time makers skip ahead, and it is the stage that decides whether the result feels generic.


1. Write a one-sentence pitch and a win condition. If you have no idea yet, use the[AI Game Mode Idea Generator](https://www.taskade.com/generate/game-development/game-mode-idea) or the[AI Game Event Idea Generator](https://www.taskade.com/generate/game-development/game-event-idea) .
2. Fill in the prompt card below. Keep the scope to one level.
3. Paste the card into a playable-game builder, such as Rosebud AI, Star, or Claude.
4. Share the link with three players. Watch them play, and do not explain the controls.
5. Change one tuning value at a time. Publish when a new player finishes a run without help.


```text
GAME PROMPT CARD (paste into any generator)
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
PITCH    "A [genre] where you [verb] to [goal]."
PLAYER   What the player controls, and with which keys or taps
LOSE     What ends a run
SCORE    What earns points, and what the high score shows
FEEL     Three tuning values: speed, gravity, spawn rate
ART      The style in five words, plus a color palette
SCOPE    One level. Only a start screen and a game-over screen.


```


For a party or co-op game, start with the[AI Game Co-Op Mode Generator](https://www.taskade.com/generate/game-development/game-co-op-mode) . For progression, the[AI Game Skill Tree Generator](https://www.taskade.com/generate/game-development/game-skill-tree) drafts the unlocks. ## AI Game Generator FAQ


What is the best AI game generator in 2026?


It depends on what you want at the end. For a playable browser game from one prompt, Rosebud AI is the most complete option. For an engine project you own and can ship to Steam, use Summer Engine or open-source GDevelop. For game art, Scenario and Meshy lead. For the design before the build, Taskade offers a library of free game-development generators.


What is the best free AI game generator?


The most capable free options in September 2026 are Claude artifacts and Gemini Canvas, which both produce a playable HTML game on a free plan. Among dedicated tools, GDevelop has a permanent free plan with 40 AI credits a month and unlimited web publishing, and Star lets new accounts build free on its default model with no card.


Can AI make a whole game from a text prompt?


Yes, for small games. Rosebud AI, Star, and Astrocade turn a prompt into a playable browser game with code, art, and sound. A one-button game such as a Flappy Bird clone takes minutes. A polished small game still takes days to weeks, because balanced difficulty and game feel come from playtesting, not from the first prompt.


What is the difference between an AI game generator and an AI game asset generator?


A game generator produces something you can play, usually a browser game with code, rules, and art. An asset generator produces parts of a game, such as sprites, 3D models, or music, that you place into an engine yourself. Rosebud AI and Star are game generators. Scenario, Meshy, and Ludo.ai are asset generators.


Can I sell a game I made with an AI game generator?


Often yes, but the rights depend on the plan. Rosebud AI grants commercial rights from its $30 a month plan. Scenario limits free output to personal and evaluation use. Meshy's free models allow selling with attribution. Star's terms state that users retain ownership of their games. Save the terms page on the day you generate anything you plan to sell.


Which AI game generators let you export the code?


Star exports to itch.io, Windows, or your own files. Rosebud AI shows editable JavaScript from its Indie Dev plan and adds project download on its $50 Pro plan. OpenGame delivers an HTML file or a 3D project bundle. Summer Engine produces a Godot 4 project, GDevelop is open source, and Claude artifacts are plain HTML you can copy.


Can you make a Roblox game with AI?


Yes. Roblox Studio includes Roblox Assistant for free, which writes and edits Luau scripts across multiple objects, and Roblox open-sourced its Cube 3D model for text-to-mesh generation in March 2025. You still build and publish inside Roblox Studio, so AI speeds up scripting and assets rather than replacing the editor.


Which AI game generator is best for 3D games?


For a playable 3D browser game, Rosebud AI builds Three.js and voxel games, and Star hosts 3D games too. For a 3D engine project you own, use Summer Engine or GDevelop. For 3D assets, Meshy and Tripo generate models. Google Project Genie generates explorable 3D worlds, but they have no rules or scoring, and access requires Google AI Ultra.


How do I use AI to come up with a game idea?


Ask for constraints, not a finished game. Give the AI a genre, a player verb, a session length, and one twist, then ask for five pitches and pick one. Expand the winner into a world, a mechanic, and a user interface. Taskade offers free tools for each stage, including a[game idea generator](https://www.taskade.com/generate/game-development/ai-game-generator) , a[game world generator](https://www.taskade.com/generate/game-development/game-world) , a[game mechanic generator](https://www.taskade.com/generate/game-development/game-mechanic) , and a[game UI design generator](https://www.taskade.com/generate/game-development/game-uiux-design-idea) .


Can Taskade make games?


Taskade is not a game engine, and it does not compete with Rosebud AI, GDevelop, or Unity on physics, sprites, or 3D.[Taskade Genesis](https://www.taskade.com/create?entry_kind=content&source=blog&entry=%2Fblog%2Fai-game-generators) builds live web apps from a prompt, so quiz, trivia, and simple arcade games are within reach. Taskade is strongest before and around the game:[free game-design generators](https://www.taskade.com/generate/game-development) , plus apps for playtest feedback and launch planning.


Is there a good AI game maker for students and teachers?


A general AI assistant that produces one playable HTML file is the lowest-friction path, because students can read and change the code. GDevelop is free and open source. Taskade has a free[educational game generator](https://www.taskade.com/generate/education/educational-game) and quiz tools. Check each tool's age requirement first, because some products, including Google Project Genie, are limited to users aged 18 and over.


Can AI make a mobile game?


Yes. Most AI-generated browser games run on phones, and Star adds mobile and gamepad controls to games it hosts. For an installable app, GDevelop publishes to Google Play once a day on its free plan and to the App Store from its Gold plan, and Summer Engine exports to mobile. Test touch controls on an older phone before you share widely.
